---
title: "New human activity (NHA) scenarios"
---

NHA scenarios tab gives you the option to explore the potential impact of two new human activity scenarios 
based on Ocean Ecosystem Accounting (herein referring to the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting - Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA-EA) 
applied to ocean and coastal environments). The assessments could be conducted in the study areas where the Ph.D. studies have been carried out.
In this sense, you can select Santander Coast, North Sea, Irish Sea, Urdaibai Estuary and Cadiz Bay study areas. The impact of this proof-of-concept 
web-based tool is based on the following studies:

1. [Integrated methods for marine ecosystem physical accounting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.indic.2026.101163): OEA physical accounts
2. [Small pelagic fish stock physical accounting: integrating pelagic systems into the SEEA-EA framework](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UD0k6_jr48X6berBKhTpq2o8N7_TC3oTDW3cty7i6Go/edit?tab=t.0): SPF accounting
3. [Eco-geomorphic modelling response of tidal marshes to sea level rise and changes in suspended sediment supply](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2024.178164): Saltmarsh evolution

Thus, it is worth noting that in some study areas you could explore the potential impact on EUNIS habitats and/or 
saltmarsh and mudflat habitats, under a set of climate change scenarios when projections were conducted. The following table is a summary
of the available impact in each study area:

| Study Area        | OEA physical Accounts    | SPF accounting   | Saltmarsh Evolution   |
| -------------     | -------------------------| ---------------- | --------------------- |
| Santander Coast   | ✅                       | ✅              | ✅                   |
| North Sea         | ✅                       | ✅              | ❌                   |
| Irish Sea         | ✅                       | ✅              | ❌                   |
| Urdaibai Estuary  | ❌                       | ❌              | ✅                   |
| Cadiz Bay         | ❌                       | ❌              | ✅                   |                      

In order to guide you where the OEA physical accounts and Saltmarsh evolution studies have been conducted in the study areas, here 
is a map with the location of OEA physical account and Saltmarsh evolution locations in each study area.

## How to navigate NHA scenarios tab?

1. Select the Study Area from the dropdown.
2. TO FINISH WHEN THE TAB FUNCTIONALITY IS FINISHED

## How to interpret impact results?

The impact results are presented in table format. Each new human activity scenario potential impact is further divided into three impact 
subdivisions -- EUNIS, fish and saltmarshes -- that represent the impact of the economic activities to the respective 
subdivision based on the results presented by the studies described above. You can also filter the results in the tables using SQL queries.

(CHANGE FIGURE)

![New human activities impact example](images/economic_impact_docs.png){fig-cap="Impact scenarios" width=75%}

Below is a breakdown of what each of the subdivisions represents:

- EUNIS: *EUNIS* tab includes the **extent (km^2^)** of EUNIS habitat types affected by each activity scenario and 
the **condition** of the affected portion of the habitat. The **condition** metric is an indicator of the 
underlaying status of the habitat and scores vary from 0 (very low condition) to 5 (very high condition). For more detailed information see [OEA physical accounts section](physical_accounts.qmd) and 
[Egidazu-de la Parte *et al.* (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.indic.2026.101163). 
- Saltmarshes: *Saltmarshes* tab includes the **extent** (ha) of *saltmarsh*, *mudflat*, *upland areas* and 
*channel* affected by the corresponding activity scenario, as well as the **expected accretion** (main driver of carbon sequestration in intertidal ecosystems), under a set of climate change scenarios, 
in those areas that the activities will be located. For more detailed information on the modelling process see [Saltmarsh evolution section](saltmarsh.qmd) and [Egidazu-de la Parte *et al.* (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2024.17816). 
- Fish: *Fish* tab includes the **extent (km^2^)**, **overall condition**, **food provisioning supply (tons)**, **food provisioning demand (tons)** and **food provisioning balance (tons)** of the fish stock affected by each activity scenario corresponding to the 2000-2019 period (retrospective).
The impact in the food provisioning service is assessed assuming that the service is constant in the entire spatial coverage where the species is present. For detailed information on the modelling process see [Small pelagic fish stock physical accounting: integrating pelagic systems into the SEEA-EA framework](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UD0k6_jr48X6berBKhTpq2o8N7_TC3oTDW3cty7i6Go/edit?tab=t.0).

***Note***: the results have to be interpreted as the maximum potential impact (under the model and scenarios assumptions and limitations) of the human activity scenarios, as they assume that all the selected space is covered by the activity and will entirely 
affect the extent, condition and ecosystem service delivery.
